userStories.title: Fleet jobs and schedules record an agent requester
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Persist USER/AGENT requester identity and make all fleet requester-dependent readers safe for agents.

**Motivation** — Agents could not be let in before, because two fleet rows store their requester as a foreign key to `User` (`FleetJob.requestedById`, `JobSchedule.createdById`) and about fifty fleet writes record their actor as `USER` unconditionally.

**Approach** — Fleet requesters can be agents

**Schema** (one Prisma migration, `apps/api/prisma/migrations/20261030090000_fleet_requester_type/migration.sql`):
- `FleetJob` gains `requestedByType String @default("USER")`; its `requestedBy User @relation("FleetJobRequestedBy", ...)` and `User.fleetJobs` are removed, so the foreign key `FleetJob_requestedById_fkey` is dropped.
- `JobSchedule` gains `createdByType String @default("USER")`; its `createdBy User @relation("JobScheduleCreatedBy", ...)` and `User.jobSchedules` are removed, so `JobSchedule_createdById_fkey` is dropped.
- Existing rows default to `USER`, which is what every existing row is. No index changes.

**Writes.**
- `FleetJobRecord` and `NewFleetJob` (`apps/api/src/fleet/jobs/domain/fleet-job.domain.ts`) gain an optional `requestedByType?: 'USER' | 'AGENT'`: `createJob` stores `'USER'` when it is absent, the row mappers (`toJob`) always set it, and an absent value means a user (so the many existing `FleetJobRecord` fixtures stay valid). `ScheduleRecord` and `NewSchedule` gain an optional `createdByType` the same way.
- `FleetJobsService.dispatch` sets `requestedByType: actorTypeFor(actorId)`. `ConfigJobsService` (its `createJob` call) does the same. The thread repository's job insert keeps the default (a thread's creator is a user).
- `SchedulesService.create` sets `createdByType: actorTypeFor(actorId)`.
- Requeue keeps the job row, so its requester is unchanged.

**Readers that assumed a user:**
- `FleetJobOutcomeRecorder` (`apps/api/src/fleet/jobs/job-outcome.recorder.ts`) enqueues no `FLEET_JOB_OUTCOME` event, from `onTerminal` or `onIngestCorrection`, for a job whose `requestedByType` is `'AGENT'`: notifications are for users.
- `PrAttributionService` names an agent requester: `findAgentDisplayName(agentId)` (new on the fleet job repository; the agent's `name`) when `requestedByType` is `'AGENT'`, falling back to `'a koda agent'`; the user path and its `'a koda user'` fallback are unchanged.
- `responsibleUserOf(job: { requestedById: string; requestedByType?: string }): string | null` (new, `apps/api/src/fleet/common/responsible-user.ts`) answers null for `'AGENT'` and `requestedById` otherwise (an absent type is a user's). Every site that passes `job.requestedById` as `responsibleUserId` uses it instead: `bundle.service.ts`, `bundle-ingest.service.ts`, `job-report.processor.ts`, `job-transitions.service.ts`, `fence.service.ts`, `fleet-jobs.service.ts` (cancel), and `approval-closer.ts` (`runnerActor`, `jobSystemActor`). The selects that feed them carry `requestedByType`, and `ApprovalActor.responsibleUserId` becomes `string | null`. Sites that set `responsibleUserId` from the acting principal rather than the job's requester (`userActor`, the dispatch, config-job, schedule and budget activity rows) keep the actor's id: an agent's id there is intended until P2 replaces the column with on-behalf-of.
- `FleetTicketEventRecorder.record` takes an optional `actorType: 'user' | 'agent'`. When it is absent, the recorder uses `actorTypeFor(actorId)` (lower-cased), so an agent unlinking a job is recorded as `agent`. `FleetJobTicketEffects` runs after commit, often outside any request, so it passes `actorType: 'agent'` for a job whose `requestedByType` is `'AGENT'` and passes no `actorType` otherwise; the ticket events of its PR link and failure comment then name the agent.

Regenerate the ignored Prisma client for the schema change. Carry requestedByType into EffectJob/PrLinkJob/BashJob and narrowed selects/Pick shapes rather than relying on request context after commit. Resolve the ticket event actor type consistently in both TicketEvent and ticket_event outbox. FleetActivityService from US-001 handles existing USER transition actors, without mass signature changes. No fleet service signature changes except those explicitly required by this feature.

Compatibility anchors: config-jobs.service.spec.ts submitEdit's exact createJob object gains requestedByType 'USER' (no context), all other assertions unchanged. schedules.service.spec.ts create's exact repo.create object gains createdByType 'USER', all other assertions unchanged. Preserve USER fallbacks for all old records/fixtures and leave request DTOs/responses unchanged.

**Scope** — In: schema/migration, optional domain fields/defaults, inserts, attribution, notifications, responsible-user mapping and ticket event actor propagation. Out: context infrastructure (US-001), route guard migrations (US-003–US-008), owner-key scheduler authorization (US-005), exposing requester type in DTOs and notifying agents.

**Interface** — Verbatim target declarations: `requestedByType?: 'USER' | 'AGENT'`; `createdByType?: 'USER' | 'AGENT'`; `responsibleUserOf(job: { requestedById: string; requestedByType?: string }): string | null`; `ApprovalActor.responsibleUserId` becomes `string | null`; repository addition `findAgentDisplayName(agentId)` reads the agent's `name`.

userStories.title: Job and ticket fleet-job routes check keys, and the dispatch effect starts tickets without an edge key
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Enforce job and ticket fleet-job keys while letting dispatch-authorized callers start linked tickets as a dispatch consequence.

**Motivation** — So a user bound to `reviewer` gets whatever the legacy role mapping gives, an agent can read over MCP what REST refuses it (review B/SEC-1), and no agent can dispatch, schedule or decide anything on the fleet, whatever role it is bound to.

**Approach** — Jobs and the dispatch effect

- **Cancel.** The cancel route's controller computes `canOperate = (await permissions.can(principal, 'fleet.job.cancel', { projectId })).allowed` and calls `FleetJobsService.cancel(principal.id, projectId, id, canOperate)` unchanged, so the requester of a job may still cancel it without the key (the service's `requestedById === actorId` rule), and anyone else needs the key (403 `permissions`, replacing the service's 403 `projects` for that case).
- **Auto-start.** New `TicketTransitionsService.startForDispatch(projectSlug, ref, principal)`: the `start` transition without `assertEdgeAllowed`, everything else as `start` (validation, the conditional write, the activity row with the dispatcher as actor, the events). `FleetJobTicketEffects.onRunDispatched` calls it instead of `start`. No other caller may use it.

Route keys (G = RequiresGuard; S = enforcedBy: 'service'):
| Route | Key | | Replaces |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `POST /projects/:slug/fleet/jobs` | `fleet.job.dispatch` | G | `@ProjectPermission(CREATE FleetJob)` |
| `POST …/fleet/jobs/:id/cancel` | `fleet.job.cancel` | S (controller computes `canOperate`; the requester may cancel its own job) | user-only + CASL `UPDATE FleetJob` |
| `POST …/fleet/jobs/:id/requeue` | `fleet.job.requeue` | G | `@ProjectPermission(UPDATE FleetJob)` |
| `GET …/fleet/jobs`, `…/:id`, `…/:id/events` | `fleet.job.read` | G | user-only |
| `GET /projects/:slug/tickets/:ref/fleet-jobs` | `fleet.ticket-job.read` | G | user-only |
| `DELETE …/tickets/:ref/fleet-jobs/:jobId` | `fleet.ticket-job.unlink` | G | `@ProjectPermission(CREATE FleetJob)` + user-only |

Every project route keeps ProjectMembershipGuard before RequiresGuard in one @UseGuards(ProjectMembershipGuard, RequiresGuard) call at the same level; remove CASL, ProjectPermission and user-only checks only from this surface. Inject PermissionService into FleetJobsController, not a repository. A refused route key is 403 permissions with no handler execution; service cancellation does its row lookup before ownership/key refusal and retains domain conflicts. A nonmember still gets 403 projects. Service signatures remain unchanged other than adding startForDispatch; ordinary start keeps its edge key. The dispatch effect starts CREATED or VERIFIED tickets only for RUN, after commit and best-effort per ticket, with dispatcher attribution.

Compatibility anchor: fleet-job-ticket.effects.spec.ts replaces its start double and call expectations with startForDispatch using the same arguments and order; its failure-tolerance case is unchanged. Unit-test the bypass entry directly and integration-test dispatch through HTTP with a role lacking ticket.transition.start. Seed system roles, use binding-only users with no legacy membership/global admin and rostered agents with scoping on.

**Scope** — In: job dispatch/cancel/requeue/read/events and ticket fleet-job read/unlink authorization; dispatch-only start transition. Out: requester persistence (US-002), logs/bundles/analytics reads (US-004), other route families (US-005–US-008), assistant preview authorization and narrowing requester self-cancel.

**Interface** — `FleetJobsService.cancel(principal.id, projectId, id, canOperate)` unchanged; `TicketTransitionsService.startForDispatch(projectSlug, ref, principal)` is the dispatch-only alternative to start. `canOperate = (await permissions.can(principal, 'fleet.job.cancel', { projectId })).allowed`.

userStories.title: Fleet project reads check keys (R10 retired)
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Replace user-only and membership-only fleet project read gates with catalog keys, retiring R10 without weakening log throttling.

**Motivation** — After `permissions-p1-enforce-core`, the core routes check permission keys, but every fleet route still decides through the legacy mechanisms: `@RequiredPermission('ADMIN')`, `@ProjectPermission` over the CASL factory, `ctx.role === 'ADMIN'`, and a user-only refusal ("R10: logs are for people; agents and runners get 403").

**Approach** — `G` = `RequiresGuard` checks the key; `S` = `enforcedBy: 'service'` (the check named in the last column). Every project route keeps `ProjectMembershipGuard` before `RequiresGuard`; global routes have `RequiresGuard` only.

| Route | Key | | Replaces |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `GET …/fleet/jobs/:id/logs`, `…/logs/:stream/entries`, `…/logs/:stream/raw` | `fleet.job.logs.read` | G (600/min throttle kept) | user-only (R10) |
| `GET …/fleet/jobs/:id/bundle` | `fleet.job.bundle.read` | G | guard only |
| `GET …/fleet/analytics/spend`, `/quality`, `/stories`, `/jobs`, `/ingest`, `GET …/fleet/jobs/:id/analytics` | `fleet.analytics.read` | G | user-only |
| `GET /projects/:slug/fleet/dashboard` | `fleet.dashboard.read` | G | user-only |
| `GET /projects/:slug/fleet/runners` | `fleet.runner.read` | G | guard only |
| `GET /projects/:slug/fleet/repos` | `fleet.repo.read` | G | guard only |

**No principal-type refusal is left on a fleet route this feature migrates.** Every `isUserPrincipal` / `assertUser` / `requireUser` refusal on those routes is removed; the key decides. Runner principals still never pass: `PermissionService.can` refuses them (`non-role-key`).

**Order of checks on every route** is enforce-core's: authentication; project resolution and access (`ProjectMembershipGuard`: 404 project, 403 `projects`); the route key (`RequiresGuard`: 403 `permissions`); input validation; handler lookups (404s); row-level key checks in the service (403 `permissions`); domain rules (409s, 400s). The first failing step decides the response.

Use one @UseGuards(ProjectMembershipGuard, RequiresGuard) call at class or method level, retaining existing response DTOs/envelopes, raw/streaming behavior, log scan/range/retention semantics, project scoping and all non-permission errors. The class-level log throttle remains limit 600, ttl 60000. Guards decide keys; controllers no longer assert user.

Compatibility anchor: remove fleet-job-logs.controller.spec.ts's 'refuses agent principals on every route (R10)' case because the controller no longer refuses by type; defaults and throttle cases are unchanged. Cover real allowed roster-only agent reads and custom ticket.read-only role refusals over HTTP, with seeded roles and scoping on. Do not add endpoint.e2e.spec.ts cases or a dedicated runner-principal suite.

**Scope** — In: project log, bundle, analytics, dashboard, runner and repo reads only. Out: job/ticket fleet-job routes (US-003), schedules/approvals/budgets/config/knowledge/global routes (US-005–US-008), runner protocol writes and MCP parity migration.

**Interface** — Each listed handler declares `@Requires('<key>')` checked by `@UseGuards(ProjectMembershipGuard, RequiresGuard)`; preserve `@Throttle({ default: { limit: 600, ttl: 60000 } })` on FleetJobLogsController.

userStories.description:
**Goal** — Authorize schedule management with ownable keys and recheck the typed owner's dispatch permission when enabling or firing.

**Motivation** — So a user bound to `reviewer` gets whatever the legacy role mapping gives, an agent can read over MCP what REST refuses it (review B/SEC-1), and no agent can dispatch, schedule or decide anything on the fleet, whatever role it is bound to.

**Approach** — Schedules

- **Ownership.** The four mutating routes compute `canAdminister = (await permissions.can(principal, '<route key>', { projectId })).allowed` and pass it to the unchanged `SchedulesService` methods. A Developer holds only the `.own` key, so `can` answers `not-owner` without a resource, `canAdminister` is false, and `assertManaged` keeps today's owner rule (`schedule.createdById === actorId`). `assertManaged`'s refusal becomes 403 `permissions`.
- **Owner access.** `IScheduleRepository.findOwnerAccess(projectId, owner: PrincipalRef): Promise<OwnerAccess>` replaces the user-only read, and `OwnerAccess` becomes `{ exists: boolean; disabled: boolean }`: a USER owner exists when its `User` row exists and is disabled when `User.disabled`; an AGENT owner exists when its `Agent` row exists and is never disabled (a PAUSED agent keeps its schedules; status is liveness, not access). `mayDispatch(access, keys: ReadonlySet<string>)` (`apps/api/src/fleet/schedules/schedule-access.ts`) answers `access.exists && !access.disabled && keys.has('fleet.job.dispatch')`, where `keys = await permissions.effectiveKeys({ type: schedule.createdByType ?? 'USER', id: schedule.createdById }, { projectId: schedule.projectId })`. The optional record fields are always read with `?? 'USER'`.
- `ScheduleTicker.dispatchFresh` and `SchedulesService.enable` read owner access that way. `SchedulesService` and `ScheduleTicker` each gain `PermissionService` as a required last constructor parameter.
- **The fire runs as the owner.** `ScheduleTicker.dispatchFresh` calls `FleetJobsService.dispatch` inside `runWithActor({ type: schedule.createdByType ?? 'USER', id: schedule.createdById }, ...)`, so the job's `requestedByType` and its activity rows name the owner's type. The ticker's own activity rows (`SYSTEM_ACTOR_ID`) are unaffected.

Route keys (G = RequiresGuard; S = ownership in SchedulesService):
| Route | Key | | Replaces |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `GET …/fleet/schedules`, `…/:id` | `fleet.schedule.read` | G | user-only |
| `POST …/fleet/schedules` | `fleet.schedule.create` | G | `@ProjectPermission(CREATE FleetJob)` |
| `PATCH …/:id`, `POST …/:id/enable`, `POST …/:id/disable` | `fleet.schedule.update` | G + S (ownership in `SchedulesService`) | `@ProjectPermission(UPDATE FleetJob)` + `ctx.role === 'ADMIN'` |
| `DELETE …/fleet/schedules/:id` | `fleet.schedule.delete` | G + S (ownership) | same |

ProjectFleetSchedulesController injects PermissionService and removes user-only/ctx.role/CASL authorization. Guard order is one @UseGuards(ProjectMembershipGuard, RequiresGuard) call; RequiresGuard's not-owner pass-through intentionally permits .own callers to reach row ownership checks. Preserve 404s before ownership checks, row locks, validation, CAS claiming/coalescing, error isolation, schedule progress, and no open transaction across dispatch. Missing/disabled/no-dispatch-key owner on a due fresh dispatch disables with owner_lost_access; enabling such a schedule still returns 409 fleet.scheduleOwnerNoAccess.

**Scope** — In: schedule route keys, owner-or-any-row policy, USER/AGENT owner existence, key revalidation on enable/fire and owner actor execution. 'USER', id: schedule.createdById }, { projectId: schedule.projectId })`; existing management service methods keep canAdminister boolean and their signatures.

userStories.title: Approvals and budgets check keys
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Enforce type-specific approval decisions and project/global budget keys, and filter approval counts by permission.

**Motivation** — So a user bound to `reviewer` gets whatever the legacy role mapping gives, an agent can read over MCP what REST refuses it (review B/SEC-1), and no agent can dispatch, schedule or decide anything on the fleet, whatever role it is bound to.

**Approach** — Approvals

- **`ApprovalRoute`** is unchanged (the assistant's `koda_list_approvals` tool builds one with `role`), but `decide` no longer reads `role`. **`ApprovalCaller`** (`{ id, globalAdmin }`) is unchanged, because `AssistantActionPort.decide` shares it; `ApprovalsService.decide` takes `caller: ApprovalCaller & { principal: KodaPrincipal }`, and both decide controllers pass the request principal.
- **Decide.** `ApprovalsService.decide` checks, after `findVisible` and before any lock or write, `permissions.can(caller.principal, key, scope)`: `fleet.approval.decide.bash` for `nax_bash_escalate`, `fleet.approval.decide.budget` for `budget_override_required`, with `scope = { projectId: approval.projectId }` when the approval has a project and no project otherwise. A refusal is 403 `permissions`. `assistant_action` approvals keep their creator-only handler (`AssistantActionPort.decide`, 403 `threads.notCreator`) with no key check; their key belongs to `permissions-p1-enforce-assistant`. `mayDecideBash` and `mayDecideBudget` are deleted. `ApprovalsService` gains `PermissionService` as a required last constructor parameter.
- **Counts.** `ApprovalsService.counts(scope: { all: true } | { all: false; projectIds: string[] })` replaces `counts(caller)`; the controller passes `projectIdsWithKey(principal, 'fleet.approval.read')`. `{ all: true }` counts every project's pending approvals through a new `IApprovalRepository.countPendingAllProjects(): Promise<PendingCount[]>` (pending approvals of non-deleted projects grouped by `projectId`, the same row shape as `countPending`) and adds `countPendingUnscoped()`; `{ all: false }` calls `countPending(projectIds)` with `unscoped` 0, as a non-admin gets today.
- The global decide controller keeps passing `globalAdmin: true`: only a principal with a global `fleet.approval.read` grant passes its guard. The project controller keeps passing `globalAdmin: principal.role === 'ADMIN'` as today (no reader decides on it after this feature).
- `decidedById` keeps the caller's id; for an agent it is the agent's id (the activity row records the type).

Route keys (G = RequiresGuard; S = enforcedBy: 'service'):
| Route | Key | | Replaces |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `GET …/fleet/approvals`, `…/:id` | `fleet.approval.read` | G | user-only |
| `POST …/fleet/approvals/:id/decide` | `fleet.approval.decide.bash`, `.budget`, `mode: 'any'` (metadata only) | S (`ApprovalsService.decide`, per approval type; `assistant_action` keeps its creator-only check) | user-only + `mayDecideBash` / `mayDecideBudget` on `ctx.role` |
| `GET /fleet/approvals`, `/:id` | `fleet.approval.read` | G | `@RequiredPermission('ADMIN')` |
| `POST /fleet/approvals/:id/decide` | `fleet.approval.read` (G, global, so only a global grant reaches it, as today), then the type's decide key | G + S (per type) | `@RequiredPermission('ADMIN')` |
| `GET /fleet/approval-counts` | `fleet.approval.read` | S (`projectIdsWithKey`) | user-only, member projects |
| `GET /projects/:slug/fleet/budgets` | `fleet.budget.read` | G | user-only |
| `POST`, `PATCH …/:id`, `DELETE …/:id`, `POST …/:id/resume` on `/projects/:slug/fleet/budgets` | `fleet.budget.create`, `.update`, `.delete`, `.resume` | G | user-only + `ctx.role === 'ADMIN'` |
| the same five routes on `/fleet/budgets` | `fleet.budget.read`, `.create`, `.update`, `.delete`, `.resume` | G | `@RequiredPermission('ADMIN')` |

A key with scope `any` on a global route is checked with no project (`can(principal, key)`), so only global grants pass, as today's global-admin check did. The runner protocol routes (`/fleet/runner/*`) are unchanged.

Use ordered project guards in one call; global routes have RequiresGuard only. The global decide route guards fleet.approval.read normally, then service checks the type's decide key; do not replace the read guard with service-only metadata. The project decide route's any-key metadata is service-enforced so assistant_action reaches its unchanged creator check. Denied type keys occur after 404 visibility and before decision validation/locks/writes. Preserve approval locking order, lease fences, command creation, pending-state/domain errors and post-commit publication; preserve budget math/rules. Inject PermissionService into relevant controllers and service without Optional.

**Scope** — In: approval routes/decisions/counts and project/global budget read/create/update/delete/resume. Out: requester-type propagation (US-002), schedule gates (US-005), activity feed (US-008), assistant-action permission keys and ApprovalRequest/policies for future approval-of-actions.

**Interface** — `ApprovalsService.decide` takes `caller: ApprovalCaller & { principal: KodaPrincipal }`; `ApprovalsService.counts(scope: { all: true } | { all: false; projectIds: string[] })`; `IApprovalRepository.countPendingAllProjects(): Promise<PendingCount[]>`. `ApprovalRoute` and `ApprovalCaller` stay unchanged.

'USER') === 'AGENT') is refused with new ForbiddenAppException({}, 'fleet.approvalSelfDecide'), rolling the transaction back. **Motivation** — So a user bound to `reviewer` gets whatever the legacy role mapping gives, an agent can read over MCP what REST refuses it (review B/SEC-1), and no agent can dispatch, schedule or decide anything on the fleet, whatever role it is bound to.

**Approach** — `G` = `RequiresGuard` checks the key; `S` = `enforcedBy: 'service'` (the check named in the last column). Every project route keeps `ProjectMembershipGuard` before `RequiresGuard`; global routes have `RequiresGuard` only.

| Route | Key | | Replaces |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `GET …/fleet/jobs/:id/config-edit` | `fleet.job.config.read` | G | user-only |
| `GET …/fleet/repos/:repoId/nax-files`, `…/nax-files/content` | `fleet.repo.config.read` | G | user-only |
| `POST …/fleet/repos/:repoId/config-edits`, `…/config-edits/regenerate` | `fleet.job.config.edit` | G | `@ProjectPermission(CREATE FleetJob)` |

userStories.description:
**Goal** — Replace global fleet ADMIN gates with catalog keys and scope the cross-project activity feed by effective read grants.

**Motivation** — After `permissions-p1-enforce-core`, the core routes check permission keys, but every fleet route still decides through the legacy mechanisms: `@RequiredPermission('ADMIN')`, `@ProjectPermission` over the CASL factory, `ctx.role === 'ADMIN'`, and a user-only refusal ("R10: logs are for people; agents and runners get 403").

**Approach** — Fleet activity listing

`GET /fleet/activity` calls `projectIdsWithKey(principal, 'fleet.activity.read')`: `{ all: true }` lists every row (today's global-admin view, including rows with no project); otherwise only rows whose `projectId` is in the list. `FleetActivityService.memberProjectIds` has no caller left after this feature; it stays, and `permissions-p1-cleanup` removes it.

Route keys:
`G` = `RequiresGuard` checks the key; `S` = `enforcedBy: 'service'` (the check named in the last column). Every project route keeps `ProjectMembershipGuard` before `RequiresGuard`; global routes have `RequiresGuard` only.

| Route | Key | | Replaces |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `GET /fleet/activity` | `fleet.activity.read` | S (`projectIdsWithKey`) | user-only, member projects |
| `GET /fleet/analytics/spend`, `DELETE /fleet/analytics` | `fleet.analytics.read`, `fleet.analytics.delete` | G | `@RequiredPermission('ADMIN')` |
| `GET /fleet/dashboard`, `GET /fleet/credential-board` | `fleet.dashboard.read`, `fleet.credential.read` | G | `@RequiredPermission('ADMIN')` |
| `GET /fleet/ingest`, `POST …/backfill`, `POST …/jobs/:jobId/rerun`, `POST …/rerun-outdated` | `fleet.ingest.read`, `.backfill`, `.rerun`, `.rerun` | G | `@RequiredPermission('ADMIN')` |
| `GET /fleet/repos`, `POST`, `POST …/:id/check`, `DELETE …/:id` | `fleet.repo.read`, `.create`, `.check`, `.delete` | G | `@RequiredPermission('ADMIN')` |
| `POST /fleet/enrollments`, `GET` | `fleet.enrollment.create`, `.read` | G | `@RequiredPermission('ADMIN')` |
| `GET /fleet/runners`, `…/:id`, `PATCH …/:id`, `DELETE …/:id` | `fleet.runner.read`, `.read`, `.update`, `.delete` | G | `@RequiredPermission('ADMIN')` |
| `POST /fleet/test-hooks/schedules/:id/fire`, `PUT /fleet/test-hooks/repos/:repoId/nax-files` | `testhook.schedule.fire`, `testhook.nax-files.seed` | G (the 404 when hooks are off is unchanged) | `@RequiredPermission('ADMIN')` |

A key with scope `any` on a global route is checked with no project (`can(principal, key)`), so only global grants pass, as today's global-admin check did. The runner protocol routes (`/fleet/runner/*`) are unchanged.

**No principal-type refusal is left on a fleet route this feature migrates.** Every `isUserPrincipal` / `assertUser` / `requireUser` refusal on those routes is removed; the key decides. Runner principals still never pass: `PermissionService.can` refuses them (`non-role-key`).

Inject PermissionService into FleetActivityController; call projectIdsWithKey with the request principal, not principal.role or membership-only helper. Pass undefined projectIds only for all:true, and the exact filtered array for all:false (including []); no project-less rows leak into project-filtered responses. Global denied keys answer 403 permissions before handler parsing/lookups/writes. Keep global service signatures, non-permission errors, confirmation requirements and test-hook disabled 404s/Swagger exclusion unchanged.

Compatibility anchors: regenerate root openapi.json with bun run api:export-spec to reflect route descriptions edited by US-003–US-008; the requested replacing invariant is only operation summaries and response descriptions change. US-001 also requires FleetActivityDto to list AGENT, whose ApiProperty enum currently lists only USER/RUNNER/SYSTEM. Preserve both stated requirements and report any resulting generated enum discrepancy for explicit scope resolution; do not assume this story authorizes extra schema changes or hand-edit generated output (see shared analysis). Do not expose requestedByType/createdByType. Existing global admin tests assert non-admin 403 status, which keys retain, so no changes to those assertions; existing membership-fleet-consumers.integration.spec.ts activity/count AC-1/2 keep their outcomes. New focused integration scenarios cover binding-only and agent/global binding behavior, using US-003's real agent dispatch seam.

**Scope** — In: listed global analytics/dashboard/credentials/ingest/repo/enrollment/runner/test-hook routes, key-filtered fleet activity feed and final OpenAPI regeneration. Out: global approvals/budgets/counts (US-006), project routes (US-003–US-007), context/requester infrastructure (US-001/US-002), removal of memberProjectIds, runner protocol migration and a dedicated runner-principal test suite.

**Interface** — `PermissionService.projectIdsWithKey(principal: KodaPrincipal, key: string): Promise<{ all: true } | { all: false; projectIds: string[] }>` feeds FleetActivityService.list; `@Requires('fleet.activity.read', { enforcedBy: 'service' })` records the filtered listing key; all other listed routes use guard-enforced Requires with no project context.

Existing-system enhancement, not greenfield. Discovery used direct reads and searches because codebase-memory MCP is unavailable in this session. All citations below refer to the inspected checkout, not the spec's ff9e39b4 baseline. The detected Express/Next.js labels in the prompt are inaccurate: API dependencies show NestJS 12 and Fastify, Prisma 7, RxJS and Vitest (apps/api/package.json:35-105); the authoritative app context describes Nest/Fastify, module-private repositories, Nathapp exceptions/envelopes, and Vitest with SWC (.nax/mono/apps/api/context.md:20-36). PermissionsModule is already imported by AppModule (apps/api/src/app.module.ts:47,141); inject its public PermissionService without Optional, not its private repository tokens from controllers. PermissionService.can already rejects runners, checks catalog scope/principal eligibility and implements .own by matching both principal type and id (apps/api/src/permissions/permission.service.ts:54-80); effectiveKeys includes bindings, legacy roster/role rows, baseline fallback and global admin expansion (:83-131). RequiresGuard skips service-enforced metadata and deliberately allows not-owner through the route so the service can inspect the row (apps/api/src/permissions/requires.guard.ts:28-57). Requires accepts string or readonly string[] and defaults to all/guard (apps/api/src/permissions/requires.decorator.ts:13-40). Every migrated project controller must put ProjectMembershipGuard and RequiresGuard together, in that order, at one level; do not mix class RequiresGuard with method membership guards. Membership lookup/access must still precede key checks and input validation. ProjectMembershipGuard resolves and attaches projectContext before checking legacy metadata (apps/api/src/projects/project-membership.guard.ts:37-57); remove legacy decorators only from migrated routes, not the guard's compatibility branches. A denied key throws new ForbiddenAppException({}, 'permissions'); absent project/access remains 404/403 projects; domain conflicts and unrelated refusals retain their coordinates. Authentication -> membership -> guard key -> validation -> handler lookup -> service key -> domain rules is the precedence contract, with service-enforced keys checked after lookup.
